I could not remember how I died but it had to be horrible. My head was spinning and everything hurt. The conductor asked me "Do you have a ticket?". Searching my pockets I realized I was wearing my best suit. I wondered if I was wearing that when I died. "Something is odd about this." I thought as I found a shiny golden ticket in my pocket. I gave it to the conductor. He gave me a suitcase and shouted "last door on the left" pointing towards my cabin. I went to the door, opened it and sat down.

In my cabin sat a man with a big mustache and another with a big nose and long curly black hair. The man with the nose explained. "We're going to the judgment”

“That's your imagination," argued the mustache "God is dead, who will judge me?"

“It's all imagination.” said the nose laughing.

This was not your typical train ride. What was going on here? If only I had prayed a bit more, or maybe if I had payed more attention in church, then I would have known what was going on. Clearly there was a theological shortcoming of mine which led to my confusion.

"My name is Benni," from the nose "Pay no attention to Fred. He is a Nihlist. Who might you be and what have you in your bags? "

"My name is Bob, I dunno what's in my suitcase.." I opened the brown chest that the conductor had given me. It was filled with money. That was unexpected. A lot of money. Hopefully, it was enough to buy an explanation.

"Well, that's not so good," said Benni "You won't need that."

"What do you have?" I asked.

He opened his trunk, which was filled with lenses. "My life's work," says Benni. We both looked at Fred.

"Mine is empty" Said Fred "except for this note"

He gave me his note, it was just one word. Murderer was written in red. We all thought about that in silence for a minute. After that I was tired. I slept. The sleep was deep, so deep I almost didn't come back. When I woke up my suitcase was gone.

"Shit! Benni, My suitcase is gone!"

"Have no fear." Said Benni "I told you that you would not need money." Benni opened the door and pointed to Fred. Fred stood next to the exit, wearing a conductor's uniform. "He stole your money. He thought he could buy his judgment. Now, he'll have to stay here a while, at least until he pulls his head out of his ass. It's Like I always say 'when you harm others you only harm yourself'"

"What happens to the other guy, the conductor who gave me my bags?" I asked.

"Sysiphus really needed a vacation." Said Benni "This is your stop"

"Is it time for my judgment?"

"Nah, that ship has sailed." Benni assured me.

"I had no opportunity to explain!"

"That's alright. You shouldn't talk to yourself anyway, people will get the wrong idea. This is your station, it's time to go. " He pushed me to the door," and Bob...Enjoy yourself this time around. "
